svg.text: Rail bus layout — 3 two-row bands, 5 straight wires, zero crossings
Rail bus layout — 3 two-row bands, 5 straight wires, zero crossings
Every hole is isolated (plated-through = pads on both faces, not neighbours joined). Each bus is ONE fully stripped BARE solid wire lying flat
Every hole is isolated (plated-through = pads on both faces, not neighbours joined). Each bus is ONE fully stripped BARE solid wire lying flat
along ONE row, soldered into every hole in its span. Bare is safe because nothing crosses: in that span every hole is this bus's or nobody's.
along ONE row, soldered into every hole in its span. Bare is safe because nothing crosses: in that span every hole is this bus's or nobody's.
Row A: 13.8 V (cols 1–16) · SDA (cols 22–28). Row B: GND (cols 1–19) · SCL (cols 22–28). Row C: 3V3 (cols 15–28).
Row A: 13.8 V (cols 1–16) · SDA (cols 22–28). Row B: GND (cols 1–19) · SCL (cols 22–28). Row C: 3V3 (cols 15–28).
All five buses: fully stripped ~22 AWG SOLID core (breadboard jumper stock). One gauge does the lot — 22 AWG carries ~7 A against a ~2.4 A peak.
All five buses: fully stripped ~22 AWG SOLID core (breadboard jumper stock). One gauge does the lot — 22 AWG carries ~7 A against a ~2.4 A peak.
⚠ Row B carries TWO nets — GND ends col 19, SCL starts col 22. With BARE wire, cols 20–21 (~5 mm) are the ONLY isolation: GND ↔ SCL must read OPEN.
⚠ Row B carries TWO nets — GND ends col 19, SCL starts col 22. With BARE wire, cols 20–21 (~5 mm) are the ONLY isolation: GND ↔ SCL must read OPEN.
RAIL #1 — outward connectors through the sidewall + jumper across to rail #2
RAIL #1 — outward connectors through the sidewall + jumper across to rail #2
A = 13.8 V (to col 16) · B = GND (to col 19)
A = 13.8 V (to col 16) · B = GND (to col 19)
OVERLAP cols 22–28 → A=SDA B=SCL C=3V3 → the only place a 3-pin connector fits
OVERLAP cols 22–28 → A=SDA B=SCL C=3V3 → the only place a 3-pin connector fits

PACK PWR / PACK SIG are the FLASHLIGHT SKU only, fed by the +Y 5-pin Y-cable; PWR OUT / SIG OUT are the ULTRA-WAND SKU only. Both pairs are fitted on every rail #1 — one pair sits unused per SKU, so there is still one rail build.

RAIL #2 — same board, same wires, NO outward connectors

The PCA9685 and TMP102 each need four nets and no single column carries all four, so each takes a power tap (rows B-C) + an I²C tap (rows A-B). Confirmed 2026-09-05.
The PCA9685 and TMP102 each need four nets and no single column carries all four, so each takes a power tap (rows B-C) + an I²C tap (rows A-B). Confirmed 2026-09-05.
LEGEND — the box style is the CONNECTOR TYPE, not which way it faces
LEGEND — the box style is the CONNECTOR TYPE, not which way it faces
dashed gold = 2-pin 0.1" PIN HEADER, 2.54 mm body = exactly 1 column (cols 1-3, 5-7 — the driver power-outs)
dashed gold = 2-pin 0.1" PIN HEADER, 2.54 mm body = exactly 1 column (cols 1-3, 5-7 — the driver power-outs)
solid blue = JST-XH header, 5.75 mm body = 2.26 columns — drawn TO SCALE
solid blue = JST-XH header, 5.75 mm body = 2.26 columns — drawn TO SCALE
BODY FACE: every connector is body-IN (body on the INNER, cylinder-centre face) EXCEPT the two drawn with a RED body — those are BODY-OUT, through the sidewall.
BODY FACE: every connector is body-IN (body on the INNER, cylinder-centre face) EXCEPT the two drawn with a RED body — those are BODY-OUT, through the sidewall.
Why this beats the woven-lane version: 0 crossings instead of 34 per rail, no wire ever sits on top of another, and every connector body drops onto a single column.
Why this beats the woven-lane version: 0 crossings instead of 34 per rail, no wire ever sits on top of another, and every connector body drops onto a single column.
Connector spacing, checked against the JST datasheet (eXH.pdf pp.2/4) — bodies above are drawn to scale in the column direction. A JST-XH header is 5.75 mm deep
Connector spacing, checked against the JST datasheet (eXH.pdf pp.2/4) — bodies above are drawn to scale in the column direction. A JST-XH header is 5.75 mm deep
= 2.26 columns, so: 1-col cadence overlaps by 3.21 mm, 2-col STILL overlaps by 0.67 mm, 3-col clears by 1.87 mm. The 3-column cadence from col 10 on is the MINIMUM,

not a convention. The driver power-outs at cols 1-3 and 5-7 are plain 0.1" pin headers, 2.54 mm = exactly one column, so adjacent columns abut without overlapping.
not a convention. The driver power-outs at cols 1-3 and 5-7 are plain 0.1" pin headers, 2.54 mm = exactly one column, so adjacent columns abut without overlapping.
Along the ROW axis: a 2-pin housing is 7.3 mm and a 3-pin 9.8 mm, so each overhangs its outer pin by ~2.4 mm. Below row C the row-4 cut leaves 2.54 mm, which clears.
Along the ROW axis: a 2-pin housing is 7.3 mm and a 3-pin 9.8 mm, so each overhangs its outer pin by ~2.4 mm. Below row C the row-4 cut leaves 2.54 mm, which clears.
ABOVE row A the board needs the same 2.4 mm — so the blank is cut through a sacrificial row at BOTH edges, not just row 4. Rows are: [sac] A B C [sac].
ABOVE row A the board needs the same 2.4 mm — so the blank is cut through a sacrificial row at BOTH edges, not just row 4. Rows are: [sac] A B C [sac].
Build order per rail: 13.8 V, then GND, then 3V3, then SDA, then SCL — straight runs: lay, solder every hole, continuity-test, move on. Then the two row-B checks:
Build order per rail: 13.8 V, then GND, then 3V3, then SDA, then SCL — straight runs: lay, solder every hole, continuity-test, move on. Then the two row-B checks:
GND ↔ SCL OPEN, and every other pair OPEN. 380 °C, medium chisel, ~3 s per junction with CQ4LF.
GND ↔ SCL OPEN, and every other pair OPEN. 380 °C, medium chisel, ~3 s per junction with CQ4LF.

PCA cable: 5-pin female at the module (pins 1-5; V+ at pin 6 unused) → two 2-pin females at cols 16 and 25. OE is spliced to GND INSIDE the cable. Both PCA boards have open headers — meter the silk on the one you use.

PCA cable: 5-pin female at the module (pins 1-5; V+ at pin 6 unused) → two 2-pin females at cols 16 and 25. OE is spliced to GND INSIDE the cable. Both PCA boards have open headers — meter the silk on the one you use.
TMP102 cable: 4-pin female at the module → two 2-pin females at cols 19 and 28. Straight through, no cross-over. Both modules are Y-cables; rail-side taps are 2-pin MALE headers.
TMP102 cable: 4-pin female at the module → two 2-pin females at cols 19 and 28. Straight through, no cross-over. Both modules are Y-cables; rail-side taps are 2-pin MALE headers.

Flashlight SKU: the pack crosses the joint on the internal +Y 5-pin, lands on a 1-row x ~8-col perfboard, and Y-splits to PACK PWR (col 16) + PACK SIG (col 28) on rail #1. That is why 3V3 now runs to col 28 — the old 22-25 overlap had no room for a third 3-pin.
